span.label: mechanisms
span.term: CONTROL AT THE END OF THE LABOUR PROCESS, NOT DURING IT. Only the delivered product is judged, so the worker is genuinely free in method, hours and place - and the same fact means the rating that governs all future work is assigned after the work is done and cannot be argued with
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: NON-PROXIMITY DEFEATS SUPERVISION AND THE RATING RESTORES IT: clients in high-income countries cannot watch workers in SEA and SSA, so direct monitoring fails - and platform rating and ranking overcome exactly the spatial and temporal barriers that defeated it
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: RANKING IS THE SANCTION: platforms do not dismiss low-rated workers, they filter work away from them, so the penalty is invisible, gradual and unappealable - continuing on the platform simply stops being a viable living
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: DIRECT MONITORING WAS EASILY CIRCUMVENTED - keystroke counts and screenshots were worked around by timing and by a second monitor - which is why the reputational mechanism, not the surveillance mechanism, is the effective one
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: WORKERS WELCOMED THE MONITORING because the platform guaranteed payment for monitored work: surveillance was traded for protection against wage theft, so the same mechanism is a safeguard and a control depending on who is short of power
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: FORMAL CONTROL WITHOUT REAL CHOICE: workers hold genuine authority over where and when they work and have little real alternative to home and to unsocial hours, because client demand and weak structural power set the terms
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AN UNREGULATED GLOBAL OVERSUPPLY OF LABOUR is what the platform connects clients to, and it is the source of the weak structural power that turns autonomy into overwork
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: autonomy - IN THIS PAPER A REAL AND MEASURED FREEDOM THAT DOES NOT IMPLY GOOD WORK. 72% could choose the order of tasks and 74% their methods, and the same workers report overwork, sleep deprivation and exhaustion. The paper's whole argument is that autonomy and job quality come apart, so reading `autonomy` as a job-quality outcome inverts the finding
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: algorithmic control - CONTROL EXERCISED AT THE END OF THE LABOUR PROCESS RATHER THAN DURING IT. That single structural fact generates the whole pattern: because only the output is judged, the worker is free in how they work, and because the rating governs future work, the freedom is unusable
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: algorithmic management - NOT SUPERVISION BY MACHINE BUT CUSTOMER MANAGEMENT EXTENDED: the client is placed in the management circuit, and the platform's ranking turns their rating into a sanction. The controller is another user, not an algorithm with a policy
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: platform reputation - AN INDIVIDUAL RESOURCE IN THE LABOUR MARKET, alongside skills, rather than a signal about past work. It is what the paper means by reputation having `symbolic power`: it is held by the worker, cannot be transferred between platforms, and determines what work is reachable at all
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: contradicts → accounts which hold that ICTs bring Taylorist organisational forms to white-collar work - the 'assembly line in the head' and 'electronic sweatshop' readings - which this study's remote gig workers do not fit

span.label: contradicts → Shapiro's characterisation of gig-work autonomy as 'autonomy over minute decisions', which the authors find far from minute for remote gig work
